run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation namespace contains a single NetworkPolicy, `deny-all-recommendation` (created 2026-11-23T22:13:14Z, last write by manager `OpenAPI-Generator`), that selects pods labeled io.kompose.service=recommendation with policyTypes [Ingress, Egress] and no ingress or egress rules, i.e. it blocks all traffic to and from the recommendation pod. Immediately after it appeared, the frontend's `HTTP GET /recommendations` handler returns 500: its child client span `/recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations` is error=true with 17-49 us durations (immediate client-side failure, never reaching the server), and the trace for one such request contains only those two spans and no recommendation server span. The recommendation pod itself is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and had successfully connected to mongodb-recommendation and registered `srv-recommendation 10.244.234.188:8085` in consul at 22:13:13.415Z, before the policy was created. By contrast the sibling path is healthy in the same seconds: `HTTP GET /hotels` returns 200 with a complete working chain frontend->search->geo/rate->memcached plus profile and reservation, with zero error rows, so geo, rate, search, profile, reservation and memcached show no failure of their own. A `kubectl rollout restart` of the frontend also happened at 22:13:14Z, but the revision-2 ReplicaSet differs from revision-1 only by the pod annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt (identical image digest, env, ports, resources), so it is a restart mechanism, not the cause; what triggered it is unknown. The two `failure-admin-*` ConfigMaps in the namespace contain scripts that revoke MongoDB readWrite roles on geo-db/rate-db, but geo and rate were observed serving successful spans with no errors, so they are not the active fault. Caveat: the authorized window ends at 22:13:25Z while the application was only created at 22:13:00Z, so the evidence covers roughly two seconds of frontend traffic and one second of /hotels traffic and there is no pre-fault baseline.

claims.text: A NetworkPolicy named deny-all-recommendation exists in namespace hotel-reservation with spec.podSelector.matchLabels {"io.kompose.service":"recommendation"} and spec.policyTypes ["Ingress","Egress"], and it declares no ingress and no egress rules, so it denies all traffic to and from the recommendation pod. It was created 2026-11-23T22:13:14Z and its only managed-fields entry is manager OpenAPI-Generator (operation Update, time 2026-11-23T22:13:14Z).

Frontend spans between 22:13:22.957Z and 22:13:24.656Z show `HTTP GET /recommendations` with status tags error=true, http.status_code=500, otel.status_code=ERROR (10 error rows) and its child client span `/recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations` with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, durations 17-49 us.

The whole trace 4f8503e42f6915a8 for a failed request contains exactly two spans, both owned by service frontend: `HTTP GET /recommendations` (500, 84 us) and its CHILD_OF span `/recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations` (error, 49 us); no span of a recommendation service and no error_detail field is present in that trace.

In the same window `HTTP GET /hotels` returns http.status_code=200 (5 rows, 2.1-4.0 ms) with a complete downstream chain frontend->search(`/search.Search/Nearby`)->geo(`/geo.Geo/Nearby`)/rate(`/rate.Rate/GetRates`, `memcached_get_multi_rate`) plus profile(`/profile.Profile/GetProfiles`, `memcached_get_profile`) and reservation(`/reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability`, memcached spans), and the span_groups for all 15 (service, operation) pairs report error_rows 0.

Pod recommendation-86cf75495d-qfkf4 is Running and its container hotel-reserv-recommendation is Ready with restartCount 0, containerPort 8085, podIP 10.244.234.188 on node sregym-worker; the NetworkPolicy podSelector matches the label that this pod carries (io.kompose.service=recommendation is the deployment/service selector for recommendation).

The recommendation container's own log shows it started successfully before the policy existed: at 22:13:13.328Z "New session successfull..." for database mongodb-recommendation:27017, at 22:13:13.407Z "Starting server...", and at 22:13:13.410-13.415Z "Trying to register service [ name: srv-recommendation, ... address: 10.244.234.188:8085 ]" followed by "Successfully registered in consul"; the read of its logs from 22:13:13Z to 22:13:25Z contains no error line.

The Jaeger service list returned for this target contains exactly [frontend, geo, profile, rate, reservation, search]; recommendation is not among them (the list has no time range, so this does not by itself prove the service made no calls).

The frontend deployment was also changed at 22:13:14Z by manager kubectl-rollout (generation 2, status.observedGeneration 2), producing ReplicaSet frontend-58f94785ff (revision 2) while revision-1 ReplicaSet frontend-68745cb99c was scaled to 0 replicas; the two pod templates are identical (image ghcr.io/sregym/hotel-reservation@sha256:1c685e1c..., env JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO=1, containerPort 5000, resources requests 100m/limits cpu 1) except for the added pod annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-23T22:13:14Z.

The namespace holds ConfigMaps `failure-admin-geo` and `failure-admin-rate` whose contents are fault scripts against MongoDB: revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh revokes role readWrite on database geo-db from user admin, and revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh revokes role readWrite on database rate-db from user admin (each with matching remove-/revoke-mitigate- restore scripts).

Prometheus reports up=0 for scrape instances rate.hotel-reservation:9091 and search.hotel-reservation:9092 (job hotel-reservation-application) at every sample it returned, 22:11:55Z, 22:12:35Z, 22:13:05Z and 22:13:25Z.

The services implicated by the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate scripts were not failing: geo, rate, reservation, profile and search all produced their own server spans with error_rows 0, and pods for geo (geo-d4c78b89b-n4dms), rate (rate-65d6967c95-mb2gf), search (search-567bb6c4b8-zsxxx) and reservation (reservation-7d77c6cb59-pvfm7) are Running and Ready with restartCount 0, so no MongoDB privilege revocation is observable in this window.

There is no pod-level damage in hotel-reservation: every app pod listed is phase Running with container ready=true and restartCount 0; cluster-wide events in the window show no OOMKilled, Evicted, BackOff or Unhealthy event for any hotel-reservation application pod (the only hotel-reservation pod warnings are FailedScheduling on the superseded pods mongodb-geo-78487c9767-d5fl7 and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-nmswg during their rollout, and a Killing of the superseded frontend pod frontend-68745cb99c-6tw6q).

Rejected: the frontend rollout restart at 22:13:14Z caused the /recommendations failures. The revision-2 pod template is identical to revision-1 apart from the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation, and the new pod frontend-58f94785ff-8w9pp started cleanly ("Serving http") and returns 200 on /hotels while only the recommendation call fails.

Rejected: the up=0 scrape results for rate:9091 and search:9092 indicate a rate/search outage that breaks the frontend. Those two services demonstrably served traffic in the same seconds (rate server spans /rate.Rate/GetRates and memcached_get_multi_rate, search server spans /search.Search/Nearby, all with error_rows 0), and the failing call is frontend->recommendation, which does not traverse them.

Because deny-all-recommendation denies egress as well as ingress, the recommendation pod should also be unable to reach mongodb-recommendation:27017 and consul:8500 while the policy is in place; that would additionally break its own DB access and health/TTL renewal, but no recommendation span, error log or metric reading was obtained to confirm it.

Validate by deleting or scoping the NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation (for example adding an ingress rule allowing frontend pods to recommendation:8085 and an egress rule allowing recommendation to mongodb-recommendation:27017 and consul:8500), then re-checking `HTTP GET /recommendations` status and the presence of recommendation server spans; no such change was made in this investigation.

gaps: No pre-fault baseline: the authorized window ends 2026-11-23T22:13:25Z and the whole application was created at 22:13:00Z, so only about 2.5 s of frontend traffic (22:13:22.957Z-22:13:24.989Z) and about 1 s of /hotels traffic are observable; error rate and the duration of the fault cannot be quantified and no earlier healthy period exists to compare against.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what applied deny-all-recommendation cannot be established beyond its creationTimestamp and last-writing manager OpenAPI-Generator.

The exact gRPC failure text of the failing client call is unknown: the span error_detail fields are empty, there is no recommendation-side log line after 22:13:13.415Z, and the pod cannot be inspected for packet-level behaviour (drop vs reset).

What triggered `kubectl rollout restart` of deployment frontend at 22:13:14Z is unknown; no ConfigMap or env var in the namespace names the frontend as a target, so the restart is recorded as unexplained rather than as impact.

Whether rate/search custom rate-limiting metrics (rate_requests_received_total, rate_requests_rejected_total, search_rate_failures_total, search_rate_timeouts_total) show anything is unknown: the metric names exist, but the range query for rate_requests_received_total and the instant query for rate_requests_received_total / search_requests_total / search_rate_attempts_total returned no samples (status no_data), and their scrape targets rate.hotel-reservation:9091 / search.hotel-reservation:9092 report up=0 at the four samples 22:11:55Z-22:13:25Z although those services served traffic.

Whether the /user path (frontend operation /user.User/CheckUser) works could not be determined: the query for that operation returned nothing (status no_data) and service user is absent from the Jaeger service list.

Queries that returned nothing and are therefore limits of this Run rather than findings: error=true tag searches for services search, geo, rate and reservation (no_data), the recommendation service trace search (no_data), the otel status_code ERROR search on search (no_data), and the traces_span_metrics_calls_total aggregation (no_data); blackbox probe_success is 0 for every hotel-reservation target in the samples 22:11:30Z-22:13:00Z, but those samples predate the application pods (created 22:13:00Z-22:13:14Z), so they cannot distinguish a fault from a not-yet-deployed service.
Consequences for end users (e.g. locust/load-generator failures) were not observed; only the frontend's own 500 spans and the missing recommendation server spans are evidenced.
next_steps: Confirm with the platform owner whether adding NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation at 2026-11-23T22:13:14Z was an intentional fault injection, since no change history is available here.

After scoping or removing that policy, re-check frontend `HTTP GET /recommendations` status codes and whether recommendation server spans appear in Jaeger, and separately verify recommendation's own DB/consul connectivity (egress).

Investigate why the rate:9091 and search:9092 metric endpoints report up=0 for the whole available sample range while the services serve traffic, so their rate-limiting metrics can be used as SLO signals again.
Determine why deployment frontend was rollout-restarted at 22:13:14Z, to rule out a second, independent change in the same second.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

data.remove-admin-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

echo "Removing admin user..."

mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.dropUser('admin');"

echo "Admin user removed successfully"
data.revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"
data.remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"

     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privilege restored successfully"

#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident.
